en: La France is feminine, so you say en France.
Le Canada is masculine, so you say au Canada.
Les États-Unis is plural, so you say aux États-Unis.
Le Japon is masculine, so you say au Japon.
L’Espagne is feminine, so you say en Espagne.
Le Portugal is masculine, so you say au Portugal.
L’Italie is feminine, so you say en Italie.
Les Pays-Bas is plural, so you say aux Pays-Bas.
Le Mexique ends in -e but is masculine, so you say au Mexique.
L’Allemagne is feminine, so you say en Allemagne.
Il vient de France. Il est ___.
A boy from France is français. France is the country, not the nationality.
For a boy, the nationality is anglais, with a small letter.
Ils is masculine plural, so the nationality is italiens.
Elles viennent du Japon. Elles sont ___.
Elles is feminine plural, so add -es: japonaises.
What is the French for Wales?
Wales is le pays de Galles. L’Écosse is Scotland and l’Irlande is Ireland.
What is the French for Scotland?
What is the French for Switzerland?
Switzerland is la Suisse. La Suède is Sweden and la Belgique is Belgium.
La Chine is China. Chile is le Chili and Japan is le Japon.
What is the French for the United Kingdom?
The United Kingdom is le Royaume-Uni. Les États-Unis is the United States.
L’Inde is feminine, so you say en Inde.
Le Maroc is masculine, so you say au Maroc.
Le Brésil is masculine, so you say au Brésil.
How do you say I live in Scotland in French?
L’Écosse is feminine, so you say en Écosse.
How do you say We are going to Wales in French?
Nous allons au pays de Galles.
Nous allons en pays de Galles.
Nous allons aux pays de Galles.
Le pays de Galles is masculine and singular, so you say au pays de Galles.
Languages are masculine and have a small letter: l’allemand.
People in Brazil speak Portuguese, which is portugais in French.
Le Japon is masculine, so you say au Japon. The others are feminine and take en.
For a boy from Scotland, the nationality is écossais.

example.why_en: La France is feminine, so you say en France.

en.title: Countries and nationalities
en.teach: Use en for feminine countries (most end in -e), au for masculine ones and aux for plural ones: en France, au Canada, aux États-Unis. A nationality agrees: il est français, elle est française.
